accepted_slice: The evidence-linked progress journal and read-only resume CLI remain readable after an abrupt task-owned Linux container termination and restart using a read-only bind mount of the current checkout.

container.final_state: stopped after the kill/restart check; no volume was created

procedure_and_result.action: Start a uniquely named task-owned Python container with network disabled, a read-only root filesystem, and a read-only bind mount of the current worktree. Run the progress resume snapshot as the container's long-lived process.
Run `python -B -m tools.verification.progress resume` inside the container and parse the JSON snapshot.

Terminate the container process with `docker kill --signal KILL`, restart the same task-owned container with `docker start`, rerun the resume command, and compare current phase, latest milestone and safe checkpoint to the pre-crash snapshot.
procedure_and_result.observed: All three checkpoint fields matched after restart.

procedure_and_result.action: Stop the task-owned container and inspect relevant containers.
procedure_and_result.observed: The task container is stopped. All existing mjobs-personal containers remained running and healthy where health checks apply.

limitations: MJ-REQ-008 remains PARTIAL. No physical host restart was induced; user authorization to reboot the host was not given.
Browser-process and product-worker crash recovery are not claimed by this container-level journal test.
The container used an existing local image and a read-only source mount; no hosted tests/reviews, personal data, employer sites, or external submission were involved.
